attackPath.dataflow: manual release input -> checkout ref -> package build -> OIDC npm publish
attackPath.reachability: A write-capable actor who can start the manual publication workflow can supply a name shared by a branch and tag.

codeEvidence.explanation: The workflow input is passed to checkout as a generic ref, so a branch and tag can share the same short name.
codeEvidence.label: Workflow checkout ref

codeEvidence.code: permissions: id-token: write; run: npm publish
codeEvidence.explanation: The selected tree is built and published after the job receives the identity token required by Trusted Publishing.
codeEvidence.label: OIDC publication job

codeEvidence.explanation: The guard checks release metadata but does not prove that checkout selected refs/tags rather than a branch.
codeEvidence.label: Release tag guard

confidence.rationale: The source selection and OIDC publication path are directly visible, and a bounded disposable Git ref probe reproduced the branch/tag ambiguity without live publication.

preventiveControls: Protect release tags and the npm publication environment.
Limit publication to release events or an allowlisted tag pattern.
findings.remediation: Remove arbitrary manual refs or force checkout to an approved refs/tags/${tag} value, then protect release tags and the npm publication environment.
remediationTests: Reject branch refs and non-tag event inputs.
Run a disposable fixture with a same-named branch and tag.
Compare the published tarball contents with the intended tagged commit.

rootCause.summary: A release identity is represented as an unconstrained Git ref at the boundary where source selection becomes a trusted publication input.

severity.changeConditions: Lower severity if manual dispatch is removed and repository policy proves that release tags and the publication environment are protected; raise it if untrusted contributors can start the workflow.
severity.rationale: A write-capable release actor can steer an OIDC-enabled publication job to a same-named branch, changing the package contents published under the trusted package identity.

findings.summary: The manual npm publication workflow checks out a user-supplied release ref without requiring a tag namespace. A branch with the same name can provide the package contents to the Trusted Publishing job.
findings.title: Manual npm publication accepts a mutable branch ref for Trusted Publishing

validation.method: Source-backed control-flow review plus a bounded disposable Git ref-namespace probe.
validation.uncertainty: No live workflow, OIDC token, or npm publication was used.

attackPath.dataflow: issue or PR text -> work item -> redaction -> prompt -> client.responses.create
attackPath.reachability: An issue or pull-request author can supply a lowercase or mixed-case bearer string when model-backed analysis is enabled.

codeEvidence.explanation: The rule recognizes only the exact scheme spelling and therefore misses equivalent lowercase or mixed-case forms.
codeEvidence.label: Bearer redaction rule

codeEvidence.explanation: The work item is transformed for prompt construction after the incomplete redaction rule runs.
codeEvidence.label: Prompt input

codeEvidence.explanation: The resulting prompt is passed to the configured model provider.
codeEvidence.label: Model request

confidence.rationale: Direct source tracing and a pinned-source local harness reproduced the bypass with a synthetic token; no live request or real secret was used.

preventiveControls: Keep redaction tests adjacent to the regex.
Review all model-input call sites for raw work-item fields.
findings.remediation: Make Bearer matching case-insensitive and add regression coverage for lowercase and mixed-case schemes.
remediationTests: Verify all case variants are redacted.
Verify token boundaries and punctuation remain safe.
Assert synthetic bearer material never appears in model input.

rootCause.summary: Credential scheme normalization is omitted from a boundary that assumes one canonical spelling.

severity.changeConditions: Raise severity if a real credential-bearing source is shown reachable from an untrusted repository; lower it if model-backed analysis is disabled or the provider boundary is proven non-retentive.
severity.rationale: Contributor-controlled work-item text can disclose a bearer credential to the configured model provider, but the scan did not demonstrate account access or compromise.

findings.summary: The redaction rule matches only the exact spelling Bearer even though HTTP authentication schemes are case-insensitive. Lowercase or mixed-case bearer credentials can remain in prompt material.
findings.title: Case-sensitive Bearer redaction leaks valid bearer credentials before the model call

validation.method: Pinned-source local harness with synthetic credentials; no live request or real secret used.
validation.uncertainty: The scan demonstrates disclosure to the model boundary, not downstream credential use.

attackPath.dataflow: issue or PR text -> review packet formatter -> console.log -> GitHub Actions runner parser
attackPath.reachability: An issue or pull-request author can supply a title/body containing a legacy marker that is included in a workflow packet.

codeEvidence.explanation: The sanitizer does not neutralize legacy ##[ workflow-command prefixes.
codeEvidence.label: Output sanitizer

codeEvidence.explanation: Formatted text is emitted through the Action's stdout path.
codeEvidence.label: Action stdout

codeEvidence.explanation: The runtime executes in the hosted runner where stdout command parsing applies.
codeEvidence.label: Composite Action wrapper

confidence.rationale: The sanitizer reproduction succeeded locally and the official runner parser source confirms the legacy prefix is recognized.

preventiveControls: Use a named stdout-safety helper at every Action logging sink.
Keep runner command canaries in CI.
findings.remediation: Neutralize legacy and modern workflow-command prefixes before untrusted text reaches stdout, and test both forms.
remediationTests: Assert sanitized output contains neither ##[ nor a line-leading :: sequence.
Cover titles, bodies, file paths, and generated summaries.
Run a disposable Action canary with marker strings and inspect logs.

rootCause.summary: Output neutralization is scoped to newer command syntax and does not model all parser prefixes supported by the runner.

severity.changeConditions: Raise severity if a hosted canary confirms a state-changing command; lower it if the Action emits only an artifact and no untrusted text reaches stdout.
severity.rationale: A contributor-controlled title or body can reach Action stdout and the runner command parser, but the scan did not execute a hosted workflow with an exploit payload.

findings.summary: The output sanitizer handles modern line-leading commands but leaves legacy ##[ markers in attacker-controlled report text. GitHub Actions runner parsing can interpret those markers when the text is printed by the Action.
findings.title: Legacy GitHub Actions workflow command marker reaches Action stdout

validation.method: Local sanitizer reproduction plus inspection of the official actions/runner parser source.
validation.uncertainty: No hosted workflow was triggered with an exploit payload.
